definition: Duty to warn is a health professional’s ethical and legal responsibility to break patient confidentiality when needed to warn others that they may be in danger of assault or of getting a serious infection.

provenance.scope: Source record D017007; pinned source text

reasons: The packet supports an obligation to breach confidentiality to warn third parties, but it does not mention a legal responsibility; adding “legal” is unsupported.
The source says the danger is to third parties being assaulted or contracting a serious infection, so the wording should stay anchored to that scope rather than generalizing beyond it.

The definition adds that the duty is an “ethical and legal” responsibility; the packet only states an “obligation” to breach confidentiality and does not explicitly support ethical and/or legal wording.

The packet supports warning third parties about being assaulted or contracting a serious infection, but it does not provide support for the specific phrasing “health professional’s ethical and legal responsibility.”
